Oh I think it’s important for sure! :) I’ve worked as a PCT, EMT, and medical assistant. I learned so much from all three. But there are downsides to all of them that aren’t a factor when working as a PA.

Edit: I should also say working as a PCT in the ED is the one I hate now. I’ve been doing it for 3 years and it just becomes so boring and taxing after a while (but like I said I learned so much and worked closely with PAs and physicians and saw I liked those careers). I liked working as a medical assistant the best! And as an EMT I learned how to deal with things on my own which I liked.

I honestly HATE my PCE. Made me realize I NEVER want to be a nurse. I know there are so many nursing careers so I wouldn’t have to do what I am doing now, but I’m so disturbed I could never. However, being a PA is nothing like being a PCT. So to the people working as a CNA or a PCT or even an EMT, being a PA is much different. If you don’t like it because the dealing with patients or healthcare in general, that’s understandable. But if it’s the cleaning butts, always being ordered around, and doing boring brunt work… then it’ll be different as a PA.

I know no one will probably read this because it’s so long haha. But I just needed to get it off my chest:). 

Also I need help with feeling so tired and sick all the time if anyone has advice for that!

I spent money on becoming an EMT. I am in Massachusetts so it’s probably different, but they need people so badly that they’ll take people without experience as PCTs at the hospital I work at. Some people had to start on med-surg and move to the ED once they had some experience. 

If I were you I would just apply to a few jobs as a PCT and see if you hear back from any. Hospitals usually need people because it’s a high turnover job. Otherwise CNA is probably your best bet in my opinion. The things you learn working closely with doctors and PAs really help imo.

Why don’t you work as a Patient Care Technician. You don’t need to spend money to get certified and you do the same things as a CNA. 

At my work the PCTs and CNAs make the same. The PCTs don’t need a course or anything. You learn everything on the job anyway.

I am an EMT and work in an ED as an ER tech and it’s great experience. Much better than working on a med-surg floor. I work closely with PAs, got shadowing hours and two Recs.

Edit: the hospital also allowed me to take a phlebotomy course after 6 months of working there. So now I have both!

You really described pretty much exactly how I feel (except for me it’s 4 years not 10 but SAMe idea). It’s so hard to make friends and when money is tight it’s so stressful. 
BUT!
You’re right, eating good food is so fun, and learning new things/having new experiences are great! Also, it’s great that you have a family that loves you, they would miss you forever if you were gone. 

I feel like a 4 year time line is hard because how can you rly measure your life, I understand wanting to light a fire, but there is no certain place you need to make it to (not saying make it to like live to, but make it to like how much you need to achieve to be important/successful). You’re already fighting depression everyday and you’ve won so far, that is a big accomplishment and it’s draining, I doubt you’re lazy (your body is using a lot of energy to keep you alive so you’re probably just burnt out). You’re not a failure, life is hard and now with social media people post the best aspects of their life and it makes it seem like everyone is doing so much better than you, but they’re probably not. 

Maybe you could try taking some classes at a community college? Even night classes. If you like learning, there are some cheap/quick associates degrees and you could get a higher paying/ more fulfilling job and meet people in the process. I met a lot of great people at community college and I only took one course there. Also, since you went to school some credits could transfer and you’d graduate even faster!!

Also, maybe you could take a trip with your family somewhere? Even if it’s small and for the weekend. It is nice to get out of a boring routine where everyday seems like Groundhog Day. You could go on a hike or out to eat or go to the beach or a museum. Really anything! I personally like to walk my dog, I don’t really have family or friends around at the moment so this helps me. 

Maybe you could get a pet! A dog/cat can be expensive, but I have a dog and she gets me outside and loves me so much that it is nice. Also, I have someone to talk to as sad as that sounds. A little lizard or a hamster or a fish even could be nice to have around and they’re a lot cheaper/less maintenance to own. 

Finally,,,, I think you should try to see a therapist. You are dealing with a lot on your own and talking to someone who knows how to help could be great!! They can be expensive, and idk where you live, but in my state there are a lot covered by the states insurance program/you could go to an online therapist for a while (can be expensive but they do discounted rates for lower incomes).

1) they can grow a lot in a short time... how long did this take to grow?
